title: Tenant action card and root cause teardown - streaming degradation
statuspage_blurb: Summary: We identified and mitigated intermittent high-latency and 5xx errors affecting streaming generation and long-lived sessions for a subset of tenants in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Engineering applied a staged mitigation (traffic reroute + scaled safe-priority pool) at 2029-10-12T15:40Z. Service availability is recovering; customers may still see occasional truncated streams for up to 2 hours while backfills complete.
customer_postmortem_summary: What happened: On 2029-10-12 we saw a sudden increase in failed streaming sessions and truncated outputs for multi-tenant streaming endpoints. Impact: roughly 6% of streaming requests across two regions experienced either early termination or 5xx responses for ~70 minutes, affecting customers using low-latency streaming and long-context generation. Root cause short: a rare interaction between the autoscaling threshold and KV-cache eviction logic that caused rapid eviction storms under a specific token-distribution pattern; this in turn triggered backpressure cascades in the serving runtime leading to request timeouts and failed stream finalization.
timeline: 2029-10-12T14:22Z - First anomaly detected: elevated 5xx and stream truncation rate observed in monitoring. 2029-10-12T14:28Z - SRE on-call paged; initial triage points to increased retry traffic and resource contention on the streaming actors. 2029-10-12T14:45Z - Engineering identified correlation between a high-rate of short-prefix requests and cache eviction spikes in the affected pools. 2029-10-12T15:02Z - Canary reroute to safe-priority pool started; partial improvement observed. 2029-10-12T15:40Z - Full staged mitigation: traffic steadily rerouted, autoscaling threshold tuned, and KV-cache eviction soft-threshold increased. 2029-10-12T16:10Z - Errors decreased to baseline; streaming truncation rare but still under observation while background cache warms. 2029-10-12T17:30Z - Close monitoring window; customers notified of full remediation plan and timelines for permanent fix.
root_cause: Two factors combined to cause the outage: 1) Autoscaling policy used an aggressive CPU-based scale-up step that was triggered by retry bursts; scale events caused short-lived actor churn during which in-memory KV caches were rebalanced. 2) A recently-introduced heuristic in the KV-cache eviction logic treated many very-short-prefix requests as low-reuse keys, evicting shared prefix entries too aggressively. Under the observed traffic pattern this produced an eviction storm where many concurrent requests missed cache, increasing token compute and creating backpressure that cascaded into stream termination and 5xx on dependent workers.
mitigations_and_next_steps: Immediate mitigations applied: - Rerouted streaming traffic to a 'safe-priority' pool with conservative autoscaling and sticky cache affinity. - Increased KV-cache soft-threshold to reduce eviction frequency during transient bursts. - Temporarily disabled the new low-reuse heuristic while we validate a corrected algorithm. Near-term engineering actions: - Roll out a targeted fix to the cache heuristic (PR merged, staging tests green). - Add a fast-path cache-warm before routing long-lived streaming sessions. - Update autoscaling policy to consider queue-length and KV-cache health signals, not just CPU. Long-term: - Add chaos tests covering eviction-churn + autoscale interactions. - Post-deploy: coordinated tenant-facing test window and full SLA credit assessment for affected customers.
tenant_action_items: What tenants can do now (concise action card): 1) If you operate long-lived streaming sessions, prefer sticky-session routing (set sessionAffinity=true in route config) to avoid cache re-warm on reconnects. 2) For workloads with many short-prefix queries (search-like patterns), batch low-latency calls or use a small prefix cache client-side to reduce calls that pressure shared KV cache. 3) If you see truncated streams, retry with exponential backoff up to 3 attempts; our SDKs will include a recommended helper in the next patch. 4) For high-criticality latency SLAs, consider temporarily enabling dedicated pools (Redwood Dedicated) for absolute isolation. Example quick check (curl): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health/stream -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" --data '{"test": "stream"}'  If you hit non-2xx responses, open a priority support ticket and include request ids from your client logs (x-rw-request-id header).
faq: Q: Will I be billed for failed or truncated responses? A: Billing follows our published usage policy; failed requests that did not produce tokens are not billed. If you were materially impacted we will propose SLA credits as part of the post-incident review. Q: How do you guarantee this won't repeat? A: We implemented short-term mitigations and have a staged rollout of the cache heuristic fix plus autoscaling policy changes. We will extend testing and observability to detect eviction storms earlier. Q: Can we get a dedicated postmortem for our tenant? A: Yes — contact your customer success manager and we will schedule a tenant-specific review including request logs and remediation timelines.

closing_notes: We recognize the impact of degraded streaming behavior on production applications and apologize for the disruption. Engineers are prioritizing a permanent fix and added observability gaps discovered during the event. We will follow up with a final postmortem and SLA credit proposal within 7 business days.
